name: Atenolol
route_note: oral tablet once daily; IV form in some countries

discovery.note: A hydrophilic β1-selective blocker developed as a successor to propranolol.

tagline: Hydrophilic, renally cleared once-daily β1 blocker
summary: Atenolol is a hydrophilic, β1-selective beta-blocker excreted unchanged by the kidneys. Once a leading antihypertensive, it lost favour after trials suggested weaker stroke protection than other drug classes, but it remains used for angina, arrhythmias and after myocardial infarction.
mechanism: Atenolol selectively blocks cardiac β1-adrenoceptors, reducing heart rate, contractility and renin secretion.
Being hydrophilic, it crosses the blood–brain barrier poorly and has fewer central side effects than propranolol. It lacks intrinsic sympathomimetic and membrane-stabilising activity.

history.title: LIFE
history.detail: Losartan-based therapy reduces stroke more than atenolol-based therapy in hypertension with LVH.

history.title: Meta-analysis
history.detail: A Lancet meta-analysis questions atenolol as a reference antihypertensive.

history.title: ASCOT-BPLA
history.detail: An amlodipine-based regimen outperforms an atenolol-based regimen for several outcomes.

safety.boxed_warning: Abrupt cessation can exacerbate angina and precipitate myocardial infarction or ventricular arrhythmias in ischaemic heart disease; taper over 1–2 weeks.

facts: Dose reduction is required in renal impairment because it is cleared by the kidney.
